newsitem.title: USA: NY Gov reports pact to let NY city issue more debt.
newsitem.headline: NY Gov reports pact to let NY city issue more debt.

text.p: New York State Gov George Pataki on Tuesday said that he, the state legislature and New York City officials had agreed on a new financing arm for the city that will be able to issue up to $7.5 billion of debt.

The Giuliani Administration had proposed the new Authority to sidestep a state-imposed limit on how much debt it can issue. The city is expected to hit this cap about one month before its 1997 fiscal year ends on June 30.

Pataki, who was joined in his announcement by Senate Majority Leader Joseph Bruno, Assembly Speaker Sheldon Silver, and New York City Mayor Rudolph Giuliani, said the new Authority's borrowing would let the city pay for school construction and for rebuilding the city's infrastructure.

"This legislation will give New York City the flexibility it needs to move forward with important capital repair projects that will improve the learning environment for our school children, as well as improve the infrastructure that commuters and businesses rely on everyday," Pataki said, in prepared remarks.

The legislature agreed that the bill for the new Authority will be enacted when it resumes its session during the week of February 26. The city and state approved five specific provisions for the new Authority:
--The authority's $7.5 billion debt cap excludes refunding bonds;
--No more bonds could be issued after a constitutional amendment altering the city's debt limit is approved by the voters and implementing legislation enacted;

The city's present debt limit is based on a five-year average of real estate values, but the sharp, local recession in the early 1990s hurt prices and the cap, which was projected to fall to approximately $30 billion by the end of its fiscal year, does not fully reflect the market's rebound;

--The authority would be ruled by five board members, who would be the director of the Office of Management and Budget, the city comptroller, the speaker of the City Council, the commissioner of Finance, and commissioner of Design and Construction;
--The Authority could only issue bonds as a financing vehicle for projects approved in the city's capital budget;

--The bonds would be secured by a pledge of the city's personal income tax revenues that would flow directly to the Authority. But the pledge does not bar the legislature from "altering, amending, or repealing" parts of the city's personal income tax.
